items.title: Retry transient failures with capped, jittered exponential backoff
items.summary: A request that fails for a temporary reason is sent again, each wait twice as long as the last up to a ceiling, with a little randomness added so many clients do not retry at the same moment.
items.details:
- The first wait is short and doubles per attempt until it reaches a fixed ceiling.
- Random jitter of up to a tenth of a second spreads out retries from many callers.
- A fixed attempt limit bounds the total delay, and the wait stops early on cancellation.

items.title: Only rate limiting and outages count as temporary
items.summary: Only a too-many-requests or service-unavailable response is treated as a sign that the service needs time; every other result is returned at once, so real errors are not hidden behind retries.
items.details: After the last allowed attempt the final response is returned as is, even if it is still a temporary failure, so the caller decides what to do next.

items.title: Retry wrapper accepts any caller-supplied send operation
items.summary: The policy does not build or send requests itself; the caller passes in the operation to repeat, which keeps retry behavior separate from transport details and reusable across endpoints.
items.details: The caller's operation is invoked again on each attempt, so it must be safe to repeat.
items.anchor_quote: public async Task<HttpResponseMessage> ExecuteAsync(Func<Task<HttpResponseMessage>> send, CancellationToken ct)
